text:
The Gift of God is Eternal Life in Christ Jesus our Lord
Romans 6:15-23
15 What then? Are we to sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means! 19 Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness? 17 But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed, 18 and, having been set free from sin, have become slaves of righteousness. 19 I am speaking in human terms, because of your natural limitations. For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to more lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification.
	20 For when you were slaves of sin, you were free in regard to righteousness. 21 But what fruit were you getting at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death. 22 But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. 23 For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

On January 1, 1863, President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation freeing the enslaved people of America. Can you imagine the joy the people felt as they were freed? No more they have to do the tasks of their owners, no more fear of beatings and abuse; they are freed men and women!! We were all once under a bondage of sin. We were trapped in sin. But with Christ there is freedom from sin making us free men and women. In Luke 4:18 it says,
18 “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me,
	Because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor.
He has sent me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovering of sight to the blind,
	To set at liberty those who are oppressed,
19	to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”
Jesus fulfilled this Scripture freeing those who believe in Him from slavery to sin and Satan. Jesus triumphed over sin and Satan by dying on the cross as it says in Colossians 2:13-15:
13 And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, 14 by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross. 15 He disarmed the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, by triumphing over them in him. 
With Christ we are freemen! We have the power to not sin anymore, freedom to not sin by being new creations in Christ.
So what is sin? Sin means “amartia” in Greek and it means “missing the mark”. It is like shooting an arrow at a target and missing it. In James 4:17 it says,
17 So whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.
Also in Romans 2:14-15 it says,
14 For when Gentiles, who do not have the law, by nature do what the law requires, they are a law to themselves, even though they do not have the law. 15 They show that the work of the law is written on their hearts, while their conscience also bears witness, and their conflicting thoughts accuse or even excuse them 16 on that day when, according to my gospel, God judges the secrets of men by Christ Jesus.
So we are all guilty of sin as it says in Romans 3:23:
23 for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, 24 and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, 25 whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God’s righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. 
With Christ we are redeemed from our transgressions making us accounted righteous before God. We have been purchased by Christ’s own blood. In 1 Corinthians 6:19-20 it says,
19 Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You are not your own, 20 for you were bought with a price. So glorify God in your body. 
In Romans 6:22-23 it says
 22 But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life. 23 For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
If you have accepted Jesus into your heart as your Lord and savior, you are a new creation set free from the bondage of sin and are no longer slaves to sin, but slaves to righteousness, bearing fruit leading to sanctification and eternal life. Being new creations in Christ, fight the good fight of faith! Keep in step with the Spirit as it says in Galatians 5:16-24:
16 But I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh. 17 For the desires of the flesh are against the Spirit, and the desires of the Spirit are against the flesh, for these are opposed to each other, to keep you from doing the things you want to do. 18 But if you are led by the Spirit, you are not under the law. 19 Now the works of the flesh are evident: sexual immorality, impurity, sensuality, 20 idiolatry, sorcery, enmity, strife, jealousy, fits of anger, rivalries, dissensions, divisions, 21 envy, drunkenness, orgies, and things like these. I warn you, as I warned you before, that those who do such things will not inherit the kingdom of God. 22 But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, 23 gentleness, self-control; against such things there is no law. 24 And those who belong to Christ Jesus have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires.
Be free in Jesus Christ and His power to set you free from slavery to sin. Walk in step with the Holy Spirit and be living sacrifices. In Romans 12:1-2 it says,
1 I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. 2 Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed b the renewal of your mind, that by testing you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect.
	Jesus saved you from your sins by dying on the cross for you and rising again on the third day ascending to the right hand of God the Father Almighty from whence He will judge the living and the dead. I encourage you to live your lives as a living sacrifice for Jesus who paid the price for you, freeing you from slavery to sin and calling you free sons and daughters of God. Be ready to give your report to God on the day when He comes back to judge the world. God loves you.

No Longer Under Law But Under Grace
Romans 6 :1-14
1What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? 2By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it? 3Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? 4We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.
	5For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his. 6We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin. 7For one who has died has been set free from sin. 8Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. 9We know that Christ, being raised from the dead, will never die again; death no longer has dominion over him. 10For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but the life he lives he lives to God. 11So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.
	12Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, to make you obey its passions. 13Do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and your members to God as instruments for righteousness. 14For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace.

In John Bunyan’s autobiography, Grace Abounding To the Chief of Sinners, he writes about his journey with God: “But, poor wretch as I was, I was all this while ignorant of Jesus Christ, and going about to establish my own righteousness; and had perished therein, had not God, in mercy, showed me more of my state of nature.” John Bunyan, author of The Pilgrim’s Progress, had struggles with his faith, not knowing God and falling into sin, but encountered God’s word and found new faith and life in Jesus Christ, helping him to fight the good fight of faith and produce one of the most famous Christian novels of all time, The Pilgrim’s Progress, a story of a Christian going on a pilgrimage to heaven. 
Christians have been buried with Christ through baptism and are raised through faith in his life. We have died to sin, how can we still live in it? Knowing Christ, His love for us, and his atoning sacrifice for our sins, the great price He paid for us, how can we live in sin? In 2 Corinthians 5:17 it says,
17Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come. 18 All this is from God, who through Christ reconciled us to himself and gave us the ministry of reconciliation; 19that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the message of reconciliation.
We are a new creation in Christ, having been spiritually raised from the dead in Christ, putting off our old self with its sins and desires and being made a new person in Christ. In Galatians 2:20 it says,
I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.
Our minds have been transformed through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. In 1 Peter 3:21-22 it says,
21Baptism, which corresponds to this, now saves you, not as a removal of dirt from the body but as an appeal to God for a good conscience, through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, 22who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers having been subjected to him.
Our conscience has been made new, having Christ living in us, transforming us and making us holy like Him through sanctification. There is a Sunday school song called “Little by Little” which goes like this:
Little by little bit every day,
Little by little bit every day,
My Jesus is changing me-He’s changing me!
Since I made that turn of face,
I’ve been walking in His grace,
My Jesus is changing me
It is the power of Christ working in you to become holy, working in you everyday as a new creation in Christ. In Colossians 2:12-13 it says,
12having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the powerful working of God, who raised him from the dead. And you, who were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made alive together with him, having forgiven us all our trespasses, 14by canceling the record of debt that stood against us with its legal demands. This he set aside, nailing it to the cross. 15He disarmed the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, by triumphing over them in him. 
We were buried with Christ in baptism and are raised in Christ through faith. Also, in Romans 6:7-8 it says,
7For one who has died has been set free from sin. 8Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him.
And in Romans 6:11 it says,
11So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.
All of our sins have been paid for by Christ and are forgiven. Your legal record with all your sins has been made clean with God. Jesus paid it all for you, dying on the cross for you, making you innocent before God. We consider ourselves dead to sin and alive in Christ Jesus, living new lives in Christ walking in His ways. In Matthew 10:38 Jesus says,
38And whoever does not take his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
And in Matthew 11:28 Jesus says,
28Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. 29Take my yoke upon you, and learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls. 30For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”
So I encourage you, learn about Jesus your savior. Take time every morning and start it right with God’s word. Read the gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John and take part in the heavenly bread which is God’s word and walk in His ways. I encourage you to take up your cross and follow Jesus following His words and walking in His ways as a new creation in Christ.
In Romans 6:12-14 it says,
12Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, to make you obey its passions. 13Do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and your members to God as instruments for righteousness. 14For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace.
You have been brought from death to life, so I encourage you present yourselves as instruments for righteousness and not sin. You are no longer under the dominion of sin, no longer slaves to sin, and no longer under law because of what Christ has done for you, bearing the penalty of the law for you. You are under grace-God’s unmerited favor.


Application:
Since have been transformed by faith, let us keep in step with God’s word. Take some time to read God’s word every day, saturating yourselves in the heavenly bread which is God’s word. You are free in Christ in God’s grace, let us not forget our savior who bore the penalty of our sins by living our lives for Him walking in love and faith and hope. In Ephesians 5:18-21 it says,
18And do not get drunk with wine, for that is debauchery, but be filled with the Spirit, 19addressing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody to the Lord with your heart, 20 giving thanks always and for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, 21submitting to one another out of reverence for Christ.

Justified by Faith in God’s Grace
Romans 5:1-5
Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. 2Through him we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand, and we rejoice in hope of the glory of God. 3Not only that, but we rejoice in our sufferings, knowing that suffering produces endurance, 4and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, 5and hope does not put us to shame, because God’s love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. 
	Eric Liddel was an Olympic sprinter who was known for not running in the heat because it was on Sunday to honor God and keep the Sabbath holy. Instead he competed in the 400 meter on a weekday and won the gold medal. He then decided to go to China to be a minister and a missionary. However, during the Japanese invasion in World War 2 he was placed in an internment camp. He suffered greatly there and yet he had hope in God, racing the Japanese and beating them in his sickly hungry state. In Hebrews 11:32 it says,
32And what more shall I say? For time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets-33who through faith conquered kingdoms, enforced justice, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions, 34quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong out of weakness, became mighty in war, put foreign armies to flight. 35 Women received back their dead by resurrection. Some were tortured, refusing to accept release, so that they might rise again to a better life. 36Others suffered mocking and flogging, and even chains and imprisonment. 37They were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were killed with the sword. They went about in skins of sheep and goats, destitute, afflicted, mistreated-38of whom the world was not worthy-wandering about in deserts and mountains, and in dens and caves of the earth.
Eric Liddel had faith to conquer mountains.
 We have peace in Jesus Christ, knowing we are justified before God. Ours sins are atoned for and we have an everlasting relationship with God and there is no hostility as it has been torn down. 
In Ephesians 2:13 Apostle Paul says,
13But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. 14For he himself is our peace, who has made us both one and has broken down in his flesh the dividing wall of hostility 15by abolishing the law of commandments expressed in ordinances, that he might create in himself one new man in place of the two, so making peace, 16and might reconcile us both to God in one body through the cross, thereby killing the hostility. 
Jesus is our peace and has broken down the wall of hostility by abolishing the law of commandments expressed in ordinances. Jesus took on the wrath of God for us where we were dead in sin, unable to fully keep the law, and ransomed us by taking our place raising us up in him through his life being made a man in Christ. So how are we made into a new man? In John 3:5 it says,
5Jesus answered, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. 6That which is born of flesh is flesh, and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. 7Do not marvel that I said to you, ‘You must be born again.’ 8The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit.
So I encourage you, if you haven’t been baptized yet, go get baptized and become a new creation in Christ, being born of water and the Spirit.
	We stand in the grace we have received by faith and rejoice in the hope of the glory of God. What is faith? Hebrews 11:1:
Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen. 
It is like sitting in a chain that is missing one of its legs and being assured you won’t fall. With faith we have hope of a future with God in heaven, where there will be no more tears, no more sorrow, and no more pain. Isaiah 25:8
8 He will swallow up death forever; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from all faces,
	and the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth,
	for the LORD has spoken.
Revelation 21:4
4He will wipe away every tear from their eyes, and death shall be no more, neither shall there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain anymore, for the former things have passed away.”
Christians have great hope of the glory of God. We have much to look forward to! A day where there is no more sorrow, no more pain and no more death, a day where we can finally meet our Maker in heaven.
	We rejoice in our sufferings because it produces endurance, character and hope. When we go through hard times, we become stronger people, and having gone through many troubles, are able to face trials with character. One grows in character having gone through tough times and especially increases in the hope that we have-that everything will turn out okay. When there are trials, have hope because God loves you through the Holy Spirit who is in you. God is with you, ever helping you to endure and grow in Him. Psalm 91:14-16
14	 “Because he holds fast to me in love, I will deliver him;
		I will protect him, because he knows my name.
15	When he calls to me, I will answer him;
		I will be with him in trouble;
		I will rescue him and honor him.
16	With long life I will satisfy him
		And show him my salvation.”
Jesus loves you and wants you to have a relationship with Him, to be your friend and the lover of your soul. John 16:33 Jesus says,
33I have said these things to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world.

text:
Reconciled in Christ Jesus
Romans 5:6-11
6For while we were still weak, at the right time Christ died for the ungodly. 7For one will scarcely die for a righteous person-though perhaps for a good person one would dare even to die-8but God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. 9Since, therefore, we have now been justified by his blood, much more shall we be saved by him from the wrath of God. 10For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved by his life. 11More than that, we rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received reconciliation.

Let me tell you a story. There was a dad with his son and his friend on a fishing trip in the ocean. One day, a storm came in and both son and his friend fell into the water. The dad could only save one. Who did he save? He saved his son’s friend. One may ask, why didn’t he save his son? Well, it’s because he knew his son believed in Jesus and he would want his dad to save his friend who didn’t know God. If his friend died then his friend would’ve gone to hell for all eternity. 
Christ died for us to save us from the wrath of God. Because of our sins, we would have gone to hell for all eternity facing the wrath of God in unquenchable fire for “’their worm shall not die, their fire shall not be quenched, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh.’” Isaiah 66:24. Yet Christ took on the wrath of God for the whole world. He went to hell for you and me, experiencing the wrath of God for us. In the story above, the father is God the Father, the son who died is Jesus, and the friend is us. In John 3:16 it says,
16”For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.”
Jesus wanted to save you, so he took the fall for you. He rescued you from the sentence of hell and calls you his friend. Can you imagine how great His love is for us? He who gave up His life for us, to endure the scorn and shame of the cross, calls you His friend and even forgave the ones who were mocking them while He hung on the cross. In Luke 23:34 it says,
34And Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.” And they cast lots to divide his garments.
Jesus said this while he hung on the cross. 
He loved His enemies and reconciled us to Him by His death and His life. In Romans 5:10 it says,
10For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, now that we are reconciled, shall we be saved by his life.
We are reconciled because Jesus took our place on the cross for our sins and went to hell for us and rose again on the third day, ascending to the right hand of God the Father Almighty who will come to judge the quick and the dead. Jesus appeased the wrath of God by saying, “not him, but me-choose me. I’ll suffer for him; I’ll take his punishment.” More than that we are saved by His life because He rose again from the dead and is at the right hand of God the Father Almighty. In John 16:33 Jesus says,
33I have said these things to you, that in me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation. But take heart; I have overcome the world.”
Jesus sent us His Holy Spirit to be with us. In John 16:7-15 Jesus says,
7Nevertheless, I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. 8And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment: 9concerning sin, because they do not believe in me; 10concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father, and you will see me no longer; 11concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world is judged.
	12”I still have many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now. 13When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth, for he will not speak on his own authority, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are to come. 14He will glorify me, for he will take what is mine and declare it to you. 15All that the Father has is mine; therefore I said that he will take what is mine and declare it to you.
We rejoice in God through whom we have now received reconciliation. In Ephesians 2:13-22 Apostle Paul says,
13But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ. 14For he himself is our peace, who has made us both one and has broken down in his flesh the dividing wall of hostility 15by abolishing the law of commandments expressed in ordinances, that he might create in himself one new man in place of the two, so making peace, 16and might reconcile us both to God in one body through the cross, thereby killing the hostility. 17And he came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near. 18For through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father. 19So then you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, 20built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone, 21in whom the whole structure, being joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord. 22In him you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God by the Spirit.
 The wall of hostility between man and God has been torn down. We have been reconciled to God. When God looks at us, He sees His Son’s blood covering over us and His love and sacrifice for us in dying for us. We are loved more than we could ever know. His love for us is found in His Son’s sacrifice. There is nothing we can do to make God love us more, nothing we can do to make God love us less. Not our righteousness, not our works, but Christ’s. In Psalm115:1 it says,
Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, 
	For the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness!
All glory belongs to God. And the Lord has made himself our righteousness. In Jeremiah 23:6 it says,
6In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is the name by which he will be called: “The LORD is our righteousness.’
God’s love for us is as far as the east is from the west. In Psalm 103:12 king David says,
12	as far as the east is from the west, 
		So far does he remove our transgressions from us.
13	As a father shows compassion to his children,
		So the LORD shows compassion to those who fear him.
Casting Crowns says in his song “East to West”: 
Jesus, can You show me
Just how far the east is from the west?
'Cause I can't bear to see the man I've been
Come rising up in me again
In the arms of Your mercy I find rest
'Cause You know just how far the east is from the west
From one scarred hand to the other

Counted as Righteousness
Romans 4:18-25
18In hope he believed against hope, that he should become the father of many nations, as he had been told, “So shall your offspring be.” 19He did not weaken in faith when he considered his own body, which was as good as dead (since he was about a hundred years old), or when he considered the barrenness of Sarah’s womb. 20No unbelief made him waver concerning the promise of God, but he grew strong in his faith as he gave glory to God, 21fully convinced that God was able to do what he had promised. 22That is why his faith was “counted to him as righteousness.” 23But the words “it was counted to him” were not written for his sake alone, 24but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, 25who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification.

Abraham and his wife Sarah were unable to have children however God promised them in Genesis 12:2:
2And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing. 3I will bless those who bless you, and him who dishonors you I will curse, and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.”
And in Genesis 15:5:
5And he brought him outside and said, “Look toward heaven, and number the stars, if you are able to number them.” Then he said to him, “So shall your offspring be.” 6And he believed the LORD, and he counted it to him as righteousness. 
God provided a son for Abraham, Issac, and we see today God’s people are beyond the number of the stars. God is always faithful and always keeps His promises. 
In Romans 4:23-25 Apostle Paul writes:
23But the words “it was counted to him” were not written for his sake alone, 24but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, 25who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification. 
If we believe in Jesus Christ and His resurrection who died for us to justify us, it will be counted as righteousness. This is faith, believing in the saving work of Jesus Christ and just as Abraham believed that he would have heirs as numerable as the stars in the sky, it is counted to us as righteousness. Apostle Paul writes in Romans 1:17,
17For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith, as it is written, “The righteous shall live by faith.” 
If we have faith, then we have been imputed with the righteousness of God, Jesus Christ, as it was said in Romans 4:24:
24but for ours also. It will be counted to us who believe in him who raised from the dead Jesus our Lord, 25who was delivered up for our trespasses and raised for our justification.
In Ephesians 6:13-18 it says,
13Therefore take up the whole armor of God, that you may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand firm. 14Stand therefore, having fastened on the belt of truth, and having put on the breastplate of righteousness, 15 and, as shoes for your feet, having put on the readiness given by the gospel of peace. 16In all circumstances take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming darts of the evil one; 17and take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God, 18praying at all times in the Spirit, with all prayer and supplication. To that end, keep alert with all perseverance, making supplication for all the saints,
The breastplate of righteousness we wear is Christ. If you were to fight in a medieval war, would you wear a leather breastplate (your works and righteousness) or wear a steel breastplate, impenetrable and of the strongest material (Christ)? In Jeremiah 23:6 it says,
6In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is the name by which he will be called: ‘The LORD is our righteousness.’
So we see by just having faith one is counted righteous, that God himself becomes our righteousness and our justifier. All of our righteous deeds are not enough to make ourselves right with God. In Luke 16:26 it says,
And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, in order that those who would pass from here to you may not be able, and none may cross from there to us.’
Only through Jesus Christ, who is our righteousness, can we cross that chasm and be with God in heaven. In Ephesians 2:8 it says,
For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God, 9not a result of works, so that no one may boast. 10For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.
God loves you and is your righteousness!

Redemption in Jesus Christ
Romans 3:21-28
	21But now the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, although the Law and the Prophets bear witness to it-22the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction: 23for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, 24 and are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, 25whom God put forward as a propitiation by his blood, to be received by faith. This was to show God’s righteousness, because in his divine forbearance he had passed over former sins. 26It was to show his righteousness at the present time, so that he might be just and the justifier of the one who has faith in Jesus. 
	27Then what becomes of our boasting? It is excluded. By what kind of law? By a law of works? No, but by the law of faith. 28For we hold that one is justified by faith apart from works of the law.


	The Scripture text says that the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law-the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. 
	In Galatians 2:16 it says,
	16yet we now that a person is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ, so we also have believed in Christ Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.
Our works is like trying to fill a swimming pool with just a drip of water. It can never measure up to God’s standards. Martin Luther, before he became a Christian, tried to walk up stairs on his knees to be saved. It was never enough. Then he encountered God’s grace and found it is not by works that one is saved, but by grace through faith. 
In Isaiah 64:6 it says,
	6We have all become like one who is unclean, 
		And all our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment.
	We all fade like a leaf,
		And our iniquities, like the wind, take us away.
We see here that our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment. A garment we couldn’t keep clean no matter how hard we try. Only Jesus can make us white as snow. 
Jesus was the only one who could take our place. He was perfectly righteous-he knew no sin and kept the law perfectly. He took our place on the cross and saved us by His great love. Our justification is not through what we do, but by believing that God saved us from wrath by taking our place on the cross. Justification comes by faith. In Jeremiah 23:6 it says,
	6In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely. And this is the name by which he will be called: ‘The LORD is our righteousness’.

We see that this was prophesized in the Old Testament, hundreds of years before Christ came into the world. Isn’t it wonderful? We are righteous not because of our works, but because of the Lord. “The Lord is our righteousness”.
	In Galatians 2:19-21 says,
	19For through the law I died to the law, so that I might live to God. 20I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live but Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. 21I do not nullify the grace of God, for if righteousness were through the law, then Christ died for no purpose.
	And in Colossians 2:12 it says,
	12having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the powerful working of God, who raised him from the dead.
	We have been born again in baptism through faith, having new lives in Christ, being accounted righteous through faith in him. So I encourage you, try to go to church and be baptized and have faith in the saving might of Jesus Christ. For those who believe and have faith, “The LORD is our righteousness”. 
God loves you.

The Wrath of God Appeased by the Lamb of God
Romans 1:18-23
God’s Wrath on Unrighteousness
18For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who by their unrighteousness suppress the truth. 19For what can be known about God is plain to them, because God has shown it to them. 20For his invisible attributes, namely, his eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly perceived, ever since the creation of the world, in the things that have been made. So they are without excuse. 21For although they knew God, they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him, but they became futile in their thinking, and their foolish hearts were darkened. 22Claiming to be wise, they became fools, 23and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man and birds and animals and creeping things. 
24Therefore God gave them up in the lusts of their hearts to impurity, to the dishonoring of their bodies among themselves, 25because they exchanged the truth about God for a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever! Amen.

Have you ever felt angry seeing the injustice in the world? Here in Romans 1:18 we see God’s wrath revealed against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men. Men who suppress the truth, knowing what is wrong and right and choose to do what is wrong. In Romans 3:23 it says, 
for all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God.  
We understand that God is a God of recompense, a God of love, and a God of wrath. God has made these things plain to man. Revelation 22:12, John 3:16, Romans1:18. God will repay man for what he has done, whether good or bad. In Romans 2:6-8 it says,
	6He will render to each one according to his works: 7to those who by patience in well-doing seek for glory and honor and immortality, he will give eternal life; 8but for those who are self-seeking and do no obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness, there will be wrath and fury.
In addition to this, apostle Paul writes of the invisible attributes of God, his eternal power and divine nature clearly perceived in the things that have been made. In Psalm 24:1-2 it says,
	1The earth is the LORD’s and the fullness thereof,
		The world and those who dwell therein,
	For he has founded it upon the seas
		and established it upon the rivers.
In this age, the creation of the universe is taught in schools as evolution. But how can it be? We see men suppressing the truth about God, that He made the heavens and the earth in seven days, for their belief in science. Models must be tested to see whether they fit the data well and in science, theories are tested as well and remain simply as theories and not truth. Carbon dating may be a mathematical model that works for the short-term, but can it be reliable for the long-term? Can you trust a model that says the earth was made 65 million years ago? Did anyone do a regression test to see whether it holds for the long-term? One must question these things. These things men suppress and refuse to acknowledge God. In Romans 1:21 it says,
21For although they knew God, they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him, but they became futile in their thinking, and their foolish hearts were darkened.
 God has every right to be angry with man. Wouldn’t you be angry too if someone took credit for your work or made a mess out of it? God made everything, including you and me and loves us. In 1 John 5:17 it says,
17all wrong doing is sin, but there is sin that does not lead to death.
Because of sin we were under the wrath of God. However, the wrath of God is appeased through the blood of God in the body of Christ for the salvation of sinners by grace through faith. Jesus took on the wrath of God, took the punishment for every sinner on earth, bore the cross, died for you and rose again from the grave and is at the right hand of God the Father Almighty who will judge the quick and the dead.  In 2 Corinthians 5:21 it says,
21For our sake he made him to become sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
In John 14:6 it says,
	6Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
In John 3:16 it says,
16For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.

The Righteous Shall Live By Faith
Romans 1:16-17
16For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek. 17For in it the righteousness of God is revealed from faith for faith, as it is written, “The righteous shall live by faith.”

Faith, what is it? It is like sitting on a chair missing one of its legs and believing you won’t fall. Hebrews 11:1 says,
11Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
All the other religions of the world talk about works, about what you do to earn salvation. But in Christianity, its about a relationship with Christ. Jesus, the lover of your soul, laid down His own life for you so that you would not go to hell but experience God’s love poured out in your life through His grace. In John 15:13 it says,
13Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
So how do enter into a relationship with Christ? By accepting Him as your Lord and savior. This is how you come to faith in Jesus Christ. 
In Isaiah 53:6 it says,
6All we like sheep have gone astray; 
   we have turned-every one-to his own way; 
and the LORD has laid on him 
   the iniquity of us all.
In Romans 6:23 it says,
23For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
All of our sins, all our wrong doings, can be covered by believing in Jesus. The blood of Jesus who hung on the cross for 6 hours and was flogged by Roman whips that had metal on the edge of the leather, His blood covers you if only you would believe. The significance of blood covering you goes back to the Passover in Egypt. Moses warned that the first born would die if pharaoh did not let his people go free from slavery. In the 10th plague: death of the first born, the destroyer would not kill the first born of the homes that had lamb’s blood covered on the doorpost. Exodus 12:21-32. So we see Jesus’s blood covers over our sins if we would only believe in Him and what He has done for us. All of us have sinned and by nature are sinners because of Adam and Eve. In Romans 5:12 it says,
12Therefore, just as sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because all sinned.
But Jesus came to save us by being the atoning sacrifice for our sins. He took on the blame, He took on our shame, He took your place in hell, while He did no wrong to deserve it. Can you understand this? God chose to give His only Son to take our sins for us and die on the cross for us so that we may live with Him for eternity. Where we will be in complete joy with no more tears, no more sorrow, no more pain, no more sickness, no more sin and no more shame. Jesus loves you more than you can understand. He took on the sins of billions of people and bore all their punishment and rose again on the third day and ascended into heaven and sitteth at the right hand of God the Father Almighty who shall come to judge the quick and the dead. 
God made us righteous not through our works, but by faith. “The righteous shall live by faith.” God imputed unto those who would believe in Him, His righteousness. In 2 Corinthians 5:21 it says,
	21For our sake he made him to become sin who knew no sin, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
In Philippians 3:9 it says,
	9and be found in him, not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, the righteousness for God that depends on faith.
God loves you. I encourage you to have faith and believe in the saving power of Christ. John 3:16 says, 
16”For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.”
